notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is
model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by is a model, reviewed_by is null); no human reviewed or
tested anything, no hardware was attached and no hardware or sim run is claimed.

WHAT IT SERVES: one task of this repository, KukaBlockStackEnv -> KukaBlockStackParallelGripSparseReward-v0, the
default parallel-jaw, sparse-reward, non-image, non-joint-control BlockStack configuration with five blocks. The
GymnasiumDriver serves cap.world.step.v1 ({ticks, action}), cap.world.reset.v1 ({seed, options}) and
cap.world.seed.v1 ({seed}); the card's other entry symbols (BaseBulletMGEnv, KukaInsertionEnv) are other tasks and
are not implemented. The action is the environment's Box(-1, 1) with four values, so cap.world.step.v1 takes
action.values[4], every element bounded -1..1; ticks is the bridge's 1..10000 bound. No driver Limit is declared,
no bound is operator_required and no site-limits.example.json is needed.

WHY A FAKE: gym, pybullet, numpy, numba and numpy-quaternion (requirements.txt:1-6) are not installed where the
gate runs, and package code never imports the clone. backends['fake'] is the package's pure Python F0 stand-in
(.fake:FakeKukaBlockStackEnv). It models the class's reset/step/seed/close surface, its Box/Dict spaces, the
placeholder observation lengths for five blocks (83 state, 19 policy, 15 achieved and 15 desired values, from the
cited composition) and the registered 50-step horizon; all values are placeholders and were never compared with a
PyBullet run. No sim backend is declared: make_env registers the id only when it is called (__init__.py:85-87,
:178), so gym.make(env_id) alone would fail, and that path was not run. There is no hardware backend.

FIDELITY: F0 (placeholder kinematic transitions, no PyBullet, inverse kinematics, contacts, friction, actuators,
sensors or noise), engine
pybullet:KukaBlockStackParallelGripSparseReward-v0 (kinematic fake stand-in), timestep 40 ms (dt = 0.002 * 20,
base_env.py:112-118), realtime_factor 0, lockstep clock, full reset, no snapshot/restore. The seeded determinism
reaches the legacy env.seed path; the fake uses Python's random.Random while upstream seeds
gym.utils.seeding.np_random, so one seed gives different numbers on the two. The fidelity gaps list every difference.

RISK/STOP: R1, above the card's R0 floor because the capability advances a simulated robot arm (simulation stepping,
MHS/spec/04-safety.md section 2.1); there is no hardware backend and no physical e-stop, and none is claimed. The
runtime software e-stop latch stops the simulation and the state stays readable; mhs.safety.reset clears it.

WARNINGS: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it records the seed for the next reset and makes no native call)
and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer seed (reset), integer seed (seed), action.values and ticks; these
are the expected simulator-family warnings. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were raised.

NOT COVERED: PyBullet rigid-body dynamics, inverse kinematics, contacts, friction, actuators, sensors, the camera
and rendering, image observations, goal images, depth, point clouds, joint-space control, task decomposition,
curriculum and grip-informed goals; the real environment's sparse/dense reward, done flags and gym TimeLimit
behaviour; any physical Kuka iiwa14 or gripper; any trajectory comparison with the upstream environment. No
catalogue_requests: only the existing cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 classes are used.
TESTS: test_driver.py keeps check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') and adds nine cases (reset members, one step, action
envelope, seeded trajectory repeat, seed for the next reset, 50-step horizon, reset options, fidelity contract,
e-stop latch); they pass. gate.digest is the digest line of the last CLI gate run; check-report.json is regenerated
by every gate run and is not part of the package.
